summary.headline: RateGain Q2 FY27 operating revenue INR745 crore (+153% YoY) with adjusted EBITDA margin 22.7%; FY27 guidance maintained, corporate MarTech down ~14% organically in H1.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 showed continued growth from the Sojern consolidation, with operating revenue of INR735.4 crore (call opening cited INR745 crore) and adjusted EBITDA of INR169.1 crore at a 22.7% adjusted margin. Sequentially revenue fell about INR40 crore from Q1, which management attributed to the non-recurring FIFA World Cup benefit (about USD2.5 million in Q1) and normal Q2 seasonality in destination marketing. Organic growth for the combined entity was 15.7% in H1 and 14% in Q2, above the 12-15% FY27 guidance band. Management maintained FY27 revenue guidance at the upper end of INR3,000-3,100 crore and the 22.5-23.5% adjusted EBITDA margin, and reiterated net debt-free by FY28. Corporate MarTech, which fell about 14% organically in H1 (close to 20% in constant currency per management's later remark), was the main drag and is the key H2 watch item.

segments.name: MarTech (over 80% of revenue)
segments.commentary: Grew 300% YoY in Q2 largely from Sojern consolidation. Properties (44.7% of MarTech revenue) and destinations (39.7%) each grew more than 20% organically in H1; the two together are about 84% of MarTech.

segments.name: MarTech – Corporate (15.6% of MarTech)
segments.commentary: Declined about 14% organically in H1 (about 20% in USD terms per management's Q&A remark). Management expects it broadly flat in H2 and is changing leadership and organising sales by vertical.

segments.name: DaaS
segments.commentary: Grew 7% YoY in Q2 and 14% in H1. Management guides double-digit rupee growth for FY27; AirGain added Philippine Airlines (July), Vietjet Qazaqstan (August) and Vietnam Airlines (October).

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: Broadly flat YoY in Q2. FY27 guided to single-digit growth, with Smart Distribution now live (over 800 directly contracted properties connected) and FY28 double-digit growth targeted.

segments.name: APMEA (within go-to-market)
segments.commentary: Record Q2 with new sales of about USD2 million, more than 3x a year ago. Over 50 properties signed on the direct stack in Q2. Middle East revenue run rate was about USD500,000 a month in Q2, versus about USD970,000 before the disruption and USD425,000 in Q1.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue maintained at the upper end of INR3,000-3,100 crore, consistent with 12-15% organic growth over pro forma FY26.
FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin maintained at 22.5-23.5%, as guided last quarter.
Growth expected to build through H2, with corporate moving from about 20% constant-currency decline in H1 to roughly flat in H2.
DaaS guided to double-digit rupee growth in FY27; distribution single-digit in FY27, with double-digit targeted in FY28.
Net debt-free by FY28; management now says net debt positive by end of FY28 (wording inconsistent on the call). Medium-term aspiration remains 15% organic constant-currency growth.
capex_capacity: Sojern acquisition loan: USD53.75 million repaid so far (about 43% of original loan), including a payment on November 5, 2026.
USD40 million of debt refinanced at SOFR plus 165 bps.
Reinvestment of spend above 20% EBITDA margin directed mainly to commercial and sales & marketing teams; AI reduces product build costs.
Cloudbeds property ramp-up planned for October; Duetto commercial ramp-up pending after partner testing.
Commission for experiences launched in beta for attractions; TikTok agreement signed and connected TV being added for corporate.
demand_pricing: Properties and destinations are growing above 20%; new property additions on the commission model continue, with churn of low-performing "bronze and orange" hotels a stated concern.
Most new wins came from MarTech, mainly properties; pipeline is balanced across DaaS, distribution and MarTech.
DMO business fell about 21% QoQ in Q2 (seasonal, July-September budget cycles) but grew more than 20% YoY on a like-to-like basis.
Management sees no impact from Google AI-mode shifts on property marketing budgets; says AI channel shift is manageable and scraping in DaaS is protected by data partnerships.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments and industries drove Q2 deal wins, and will this win pace continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Most wins came from MarTech properties (hotels); pipeline is balanced across DaaS, distribution and MarTech. Management credited cross-sell in APMEA (team grew from about 15 to 100 people) and a global key accounts team for the top 10 accounts.

qa_highlights.question: How does organic growth reach 15% constant currency from roughly 9-10% normalised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said arresting the corporate decline could add about 200-300 bps, and properties and destinations (over 80% of MarTech, growing above 20%) could accelerate further if churn is reduced.

qa_highlights.question: How should margins be treated given team build-out?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is comfortable with anything above 20% and will reinvest above that, mainly in commercial and sales teams; AI is lowering the cost of product build.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 revenue guidance dependent on a DMO recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H2 growth also depends on corporate moving from about 20% constant-currency decline in H1 to flattish, alongside DMO seasonal recovery in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is margin expansion linked to currency?
qa_highlights.answer: Chetan Garg said currency benefit is not meaningful because most revenue and cost is USD-based; Bhanu Chopra attributed margin gains to cost synergies from merging Sojern and Adara platforms and shared HR and finance services.

qa_highlights.question: Does AI pose a fundamental risk to DaaS?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no, citing anti-blocking technology, formal data partnerships with subscribers, and data purchases; monetisation is per data volume regardless of channel (APIs or LLM interfaces such as Claude or ChatGPT via MCP).

risks_watch: Corporate MarTech: H1 decline of about 14% organically (about 20% in USD) must flatten in H2 for guidance; management acknowledged the segment was deprioritised under Sojern.
Middle East: revenue run rate still about 48% below pre-disruption levels (USD500,000 vs USD970,000 a month); management called it a continuing headwind.
Property churn: pay-for-performance model with low-performing hotels churning; management expects the integrated stack to reduce it, unproven so far.
Q3 and Q4 must grow sequentially to reach the upper end of INR3,100 crore, which depends on DMO seasonal recovery and corporate stabilisation.
Cash flow: H1 EBITDA-to-FCF conversion of 87% was flattered by one-time Sojern collections; net debt-free timing needs watching.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the core MarTech properties and destinations business and APMEA, but candid and cautious on corporate MarTech, which management says needs fixing. Some answers on AI, Europe and pipeline were hedged or unclear, and the call contained several numeric inconsistencies (INR735.4 vs INR745 crore revenue, and "net debt-free" vs "net debt positive" by FY28).
key_quotes: We are maintaining our guidance of revenue that we expect to be at the upper end of the INR3,000 crore-INR3,100 crores range that we had shared in the beginning of the year.
Our medium-term aspiration remains 15% organic growth, constant currency year-on-year growth.

The margin expansion that you have seen is not a result of anything to do with currency. It's really the cost synergies that we were able to realize as a result of taking all the platforms that we had, especially Sojern and Adara, and make it into one platform.
We only get paid if we deliver bookings for our customers, so it's an outcome-based model.

growth.why: FY27 revenue held at upper end of INR3,000-3,100 crore (about 12-15% organic growth), backed by partial evidence: properties and destinations up over 20% organically in H1, APMEA new sales about 3x YoY, and DaaS/distribution guidance, with no specific new capacity or order-book figures; corporate MarTech is the H2 risk.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Corporate MarTech fell about 14% organically in H1 (about 20% in USD) and must be roughly flat in H2; Middle East run rate USD500,000/month is about 48% below pre-disruption USD970,000.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Commission for experiences in beta for attractions, TikTok agreement signed with connected TV being added for corporate, and Cloudbeds property ramp planned for October.

rows.label: APMEA cross-sell momentum
rows.why: Record Q2 APMEA new sales of about USD2 million, more than 3x a year ago, with over 50 properties signed on the direct stack and team grown from about 15 to 100 people.

rows.label: DaaS airline wins
rows.why: DaaS grew 7% in Q2 and 14% in H1, with Philippine Airlines (July), Vietjet Qazaqstan (August) and Vietnam Airlines (October) added; FY27 guided to double-digit rupee growth.

rows.label: Net debt-free by FY28
rows.why: Net debt INR494 crore at Sep 30 with USD53.75m of Sojern loan repaid; management says net debt-free by FY28 but wording was inconsistent on the call, and H1 FCF was flattered by one-time collections.

tone.note: Management was confident on properties, destinations and APMEA but cautious on corporate MarTech and the Middle East; analysts pushed on how 15% constant-currency growth is reached from a roughly 9-10% normalised base, and the call had numeric inconsistencies on revenue and net debt timing.
